note: Measured on Windows 11 26H2 (build 26300), 2560x1600 @150% scaling, release build 0.1.0 after the reviewed-install / runtime-action / panel-warm-keep work. WebView2 processes are counted only when they are descendants of the host process; other applications on the machine have their own WebView2 instances and must not be included. The panel warm-keep teardown was measured with a 6 s override (TOOLBOX_PANEL_WARM_SECS) to avoid a 5 minute wait; the shipped default is 300 s.

measurements.state: panel hidden, still warm (reopen is instant)
panel warm window destroyed (teardown after warm TTL)

observations: The idle target (<=30 MB) is met with a wide margin: 11.7 MB with zero WebView2 processes, because the floating ball is a native layered window and no webview exists until a window is opened.
The first window costs ~320 MB of WebView2 processes. This is the fixed price of the Chromium engine (browser + GPU + renderer + utility processes) and is not reducible by application code.
Closing a tool window destroys its webview and releases those processes again (verified by re-running the idle measurement).

The panel is deliberately kept warm for 5 minutes after hiding so reopening is instant; during that window it still owns its six WebView2 processes. The teardown timer then destroys the webview and the child processes disappear.

After the panel teardown the host working set stays above the pre-webview idle number (24.4 MB vs 11.7 MB) because WebView2 loader/DLL pages remain mapped in the process; private bytes stay low (4.8 MB vs 2.2 MB) and CPU is 0%, so nothing is spinning or leaking. A restart returns the process to the 11.7 MB baseline.
